findings.F1: The tested result points the way the idea predicts but stays short of the bar, because the small rises dilute it. At 5 days on folds B and C, the unusual move rises steadily across the quartiles of the one-day rise in 30-day standard deviations: -0.05 % (t -0.02, 43 days), +1.08 % (t 0.61, 47 days), +1.92 % (t 1.05, 43 days), +3.01 % (t 2.03, 37 days). Strength runs from 0.01 to 0.22, so the effect is carried by the largest rises.
findings.F2: The give-back shows most clearly over the next day. At 1 day the unusual move is +0.85 % (t 1.97, 235 days, 639 cases) with a strength of 0.157. Over 5 days it is +1.49 % (t 1.26, 121 days) with a strength of 0.118. The 1-day total move of +0.67 % is about 3 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade, while the tested 5-day total move is +0.00 %.
findings.F3: The effect varies by period, which keeps the pooled t low. At 5 days the unusual move is positive in 2018 (+1.62 %, t 0.57), 2019 (+2.13 %, t 2.55) and 2021 (+3.48 %, t 1.33), but negative in 2020 (-1.21 %, t -0.81). Windows range from -2.06 % (w17) to +4.52 % (w18).
findings.F4: The brief's own situation, a rise over several days, shows no give-back.
findings.F5: The tested idea already ran on all 19 coins and all four folds of daily data, so no more daily data is available to repeat it unchanged.

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger the fall in its price over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would short a sharp up day in a falling, agitated market for one day only, when most of the give-back happens and the move covers the trade's cost.
ideas.name: one-day rise fades next day

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger the fall in its price over the next 5 days, only when that rise is larger than the coin's usual daily swing over the past 30 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would short only the up days that stand out against the coin's usual swing in a falling, agitated market, and leave the ordinary up days alone.
ideas.name: large one-day rises fade
